artworks.title: Acis and Galatea
artworks.description: Giordano's Baroque canvas stages Ovid's Sicilian pastoral at the fatal instant: the nereid Galatea embraces the shepherd Acis while the jealous Cyclops Polyphemus looms with the rock that will crush him. Held by the Fondation Bemberg, Toulouse, it is one of the fullest painted tellings of the love triangle that ends with Acis transformed into a river.

artworks.title: Acis and Galatea
artworks.description: Perrier's French Classical painting pairs the shepherd Acis with Galatea against a coastal setting, freezing the idyll before Polyphemus' jealous violence. The canvas is in the Musée des Beaux-Arts de Carcassonne.

artworks.title: Acis and Galatea
artworks.description: Tischbein's Rococo treatment of Ovid's lovers keeps Acis and Galatea in a soft pastoral embrace, the Sicilian myth translated into eighteenth-century elegance before the Cyclops' rock falls.

artworks.title: Acis and Galatea
artworks.description: Guillemot's Neoclassical canvas returns to the Sicilian shore: Acis and Galatea as Ovid's doomed couple, the pastoral calm already shadowed by Polyphemus' approaching jealousy.

music.title: Acis and Galatea
music.description: Handel's pastoral masque stages the Sicilian shepherd crushed by Polyphemus — Acis as English Baroque's favourite rustic martyr.

popCulture.title: Acis and Galatea
popCulture.description: The lovers' Sicilian tragedy endures as Ovid's pastoral triangle — Acis, Galatea and the jealous Cyclops.
